mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 4.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points over three months signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in >60% of instances when UNRATE rises >0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicate broad economic contraction in consumer demand and manufacturing output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in >60% of instances when both HOUST and INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 3.0% annualized) during late-cycle expansions indicates stretched valuations and reduced margin for error, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 3.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in >60% of instances when PAYEMS growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) and unemployment rate (UNRATE > 4.8%) indicate aggressive monetary tightening coinciding with labor market weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS >4.5% and UNRATE >4.8%.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO above 3.0% annualized) signals robust manufacturing output supporting corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in >60% of instances when INDPRO growth exceeds 3.0% annualized.
